question.worked_solution:
First, we write $3\,\frac{3}{4}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
3\,\frac{3}{4}=\frac{(3\times 4)+3}{4}=\frac{15}{4}
$$

We also write  $2\,\frac{2}{5}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
2\,\frac{2}{5}=\frac{(2\times 5)+2}{5}=\frac{12}{5}
$$

Now, we can multiply the two numbers. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{15}{4}\times \frac{12}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify this product by swapping the denominators:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{15}{4}\times \frac{12}{5} & =\frac{15}{5}\times \frac{12}{4} \\  & =3\times 3 \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
3\,\frac{3}{4}\times 2\,\frac{2}{5}=9
$$
